issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a male torture survivor, sexual-trauma-specific verbal cues are possible only if sexual torture or sexual humiliation is part of the trauma, but the rest of the profile provides no corresponding sexual content in memory, appraisals, threat, or coping. As selected, this trigger appears disconnected from the trauma representation and is hard to justify clinically.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: The appraisal that others can visibly see what happened to him implies shame/marked visible contamination or exposure. That could occur after torture, but here it is not supported by the memory items, trigger content, or other appraisals, making it feel mismatched with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Gambling: I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
issues.explanation: Gambling as a coping strategy is not impossible, but in this profile it is poorly linked to the active formulation. The main connected pattern is triggers ↔ negative appraisals with memory-linked re-experiencing and threat-driven compliance/detachment. Gambling introduces a separate excitement-seeking coping style that is not reflected elsewhere and feels clinically disconnected rather than integrated.

vignette: Seventy-year-old Miguel, a widowed Latin American man and retired welder, has been haunted by his traumatic past for years. His experiences of torture have left him with deeply ingrained triggers that repeatedly disrupt his daily life. The sound of gunfire, a sense of entrapment, and any sign of violence can instantly transport him back to the horror he endured. When Miguel encounters these triggers, he often feels as though there are no options for escape or relief. The sound of gunfire, in particular, serves as an intensely distressing reminder of his torture. Recently, while working part-time at a local metal shop, the loud noise from another worker accidentally discharging a pistol sent him into a state of shock and panic. This triggered a series of coping mechanisms he had developed over time. Miguel would detach himself emotionally from the memories, trying to distance himself from the traumatic event. He also became overly compliant whenever he felt threatened, often agreeing with others just to avoid further harm. When Miguel tries to recount what happened during his torture, he struggles to explain clearly and loses track of his thoughts mid-sentence. The memory feels as though it is happening right now rather than something that occurred in the past. This sense of immediacy has made him feel trapped by his experiences. He often finds himself feeling intense rage when he recalls these events. Miguel’s fear that harm can come from anyone and anywhere has significantly impacted how he navigates daily life. The belief that he could have done more to stop what happened, coupled with feelings of self-blame, exacerbates his emotional distress. These negative appraisals lead him to suppress thoughts about the trauma, as they only deepen his sense of guilt and fear. His maladaptive strategies often stem from these negative beliefs. Miguel believes that he can never know who will harm him, which makes it nearly impossible for him to feel safe in any situation. This constant vigilance has led to a series of avoidance behaviors where he tries not to think about the trauma at all. However, this suppression only serves to intensify his triggers and keeps the memory vividly present. The weight of these negative appraisals has become overwhelming, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that Miguel struggles to break. He is certain that if he were more proactive or acted differently during his torture, things would have turned out differently. This belief feeds into his maladaptive strategies, further complicating his ability to process and cope with the trauma. The combination of triggers, memory distortions, negative appraisals, and maladaptive coping mechanisms has led Miguel to a point where he feels trapped in a cycle of fear and guilt that permeates every aspect of his life. His attempts to avoid these painful memories have only made them more potent, as he finds himself constantly reacting to reminders and triggers. Miguel finally decided to seek help after an incident at work triggered a particularly severe episode. He realized that he could no longer continue living in fear and wanted support to break this cycle. What frightened him most was the prospect of never finding peace or understanding from his experiences, but what he hoped for was a chance to reclaim his life and find some form of healing.
